title: Cabled panel baby blanket
subtitle: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket with a central cable column flanked by seed stitch, at aran weight.
excerpt: A 75 by 90 cm cot blanket in aran weight on 5 mm needles, featuring a central twelve-stitch cable column flanked by seed-stitch side panels. The cable introduces a new technique without adding complexity to the overall construction. About 280 g of aran.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 10th series (1894), §Cable Stitch Baby Wraps, gives a cabled nursery blanket using a central cable column flanked by moss stitch. The four-stitch cable-front and cable-back crossings are documented in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Cable Stitches.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rows = 10 × 10 cm in seed stitch on 5 mm needles. The cable panel draws in slightly; see notes.

stitchCountCheckpoints.label: Halfway check — 137 sts total, about 45 cm

glossaryTerms.definition: A manoeuvre that crosses a group of stitches over another group to produce a twisted rope effect. Stitches are transferred to a cable needle, held to the front or back, the remaining stitches are knitted, and the held stitches are then knitted. Front-held crosses slant to the left; back-held crosses slant to the right.

A flat-lying stitch pattern produced by alternating knit and purl stitches. On the next row, the knit stitches are purled and the purl stitches are knitted, creating a pebbly surface. Seed stitch lies flat without blocking and is reversible.

content.text: A single-panel rectangle worked flat on 5 mm needles, finishing at 75 cm wide by 90 cm long. The blanket has a central twelve-stitch column of
cable cross
flanked by
seed stitch
side panels.

A single panel avoids seaming. The cable column was centred over seed stitch so the fabric lies flat: seed stitch has minimal tendency to curl and frames the cable without a garter border. Aran weight was chosen over DK because the cable reads more boldly at a larger stitch size, and the blanket works up faster. Budget about 280 g (about 500 m / 545 yards) of aran yarn. Buy in matched dye lots. A cable needle is required; use a straight or kinked cable needle in a size close to 5 mm.
What you need

items.name: Yarn
items.qty: 280 g (about 500 m / 545 yards) of aran-weight yarn

items.name: Needles
items.qty: 5 mm (UK 6 / US 8) circular needle, 80 cm or longer

content.text: Gauge

18 stitches and 24 rows to 10 cm in seed stitch on 5 mm needles, unblocked. The cable panel draws in by about 2 cm relative to the same stitch count in seed stitch. The pattern accounts for this by using 137 stitches (seed 62 + cable 12 + seed 62 + 1 edge stitch each side).
If your seed-stitch gauge is 16 stitches per 10 cm, the blanket will be about 84 cm wide. Adjust the seed-stitch panels by adding or removing stitches in multiples of 2.
Stitches used

items.name: C4F
items.qty: cable 4 front: slip 2 to cable needle, hold front, k2, k2 from cable needle

items.name: C4B
items.qty: cable 4 back: slip 2 to cable needle, hold back, k2, k2 from cable needle

items.name: seed
items.qty: k1, p1 alternating; on return rows k the purls and p the knits

content.text: Pattern
Cast-on

Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 137 stitches. Long-tail tail: (5 × 137) / 10 + 15 = 68.5 + 15 = 84 cm. Measure 100 cm of tail. Place markers after stitch 62 and before stitch 75 to mark the 12-stitch cable zone.
Body
All rows: work 62 sts in seed stitch, slip marker, work the cable panel, slip marker, work 62 sts in seed stitch.
Cable panel (12 sts), RS cable rows (every 8 rows starting at row 5): k2, C4B, C4F, k2.
Cable panel on all other rows (RS and WS): k12 on RS, p12 on WS.
Continue until the blanket measures 90 cm. When you set this aside, note whether the next cable row is due (cable rows occur every 8 rows; mark the count on a sticky note).
Stitch count check-ins
At row 108 (about 45 cm): count across. You should have 137 stitches total: 62 in each seed panel and 12 in the cable. At row 214 (about 89.5 cm): count again before casting off.
Common faults

Cable crossing in the wrong direction: C4F and C4B were swapped. Hold the cable needle firmly to the front before knitting to confirm the direction. The cable should show as a spiral; two adjacent crossings slanting in opposite directions is the result of alternating F and B at random.
Dropped stitches from the cable needle: the cable needle fell and pulled stitches with it. Use a bent or kinked cable needle that grips stitches. Work in a seated position with the work in your lap.

Seed stitch reverting to rib: on the return row the wrong stitches were knitted instead of purled. Read the stitch on the needle each row: if it presents as a knit stitch (V-shape), purl it; if it presents as a purl bump, knit it.
Cast-off
Cast off in pattern: seed stitch panels cast off k1p1 alternating, cable panel cast off knitwise. Use a relaxed tension.
Finishing
Weave in both ends on the wrong side. Blocking is optional: a light wet block will open the cable column; the seed-stitch panels need no blocking to lie flat.
Care
Machine wash on a gentle 30-degree cycle for superwash aran. Lay flat to dry. Cables lose some definition if tumble-dried at high heat.
What to try next

From a single central cable, the progression is a multi-cable blanket with three or five cable columns separated by narrow seed-stitch columns. The technique is identical; only the number of marked zones increases.
